title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第3部分：变化

chapters.Jacobian: 3. 会弯曲的映射：雅可比矩阵
chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现

37d8f822b29f.en: In part one we worked out a single derivative by hand: the gradient of the surprise with respect to the scores, the model's guess minus the truth. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2 has a hundred and twenty-four million numbers. Qwen3-4B has four billion. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every step of training needs the derivative of the loss with respect to every single one of them, and nobody works those out by hand.
37d8f822b29f.zh: 在第1部分，我们亲手算出了一个导数：意外度对各个分数的梯度，也就是模型的猜测，减去真相。<bookmark mark='a'/>GPT-2有1.24亿个数。Qwen3-4B有40亿个。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练的每一步，都需要损失对其中每一个数的导数，而这些导数，谁也不会去手算。

e9fbac03e13e.en: This part builds the machine that does it. It's a single idea, the chain rule run backwards, and it fits in a few pages of code. <bookmark mark='a'/> We'll build it, check it, and train a model with it on part one's books.
e9fbac03e13e.zh: 这一部分，就来搭建做这件事的机器。它只有一个想法：倒过来运行的链式法则，写成代码，几页就装得下。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会把它搭起来，检验它，再用它在第1部分的那些书上训练一个模型。

a9c2ef9a22eb.en: Zoom in on a smooth curve, closer and closer, <bookmark mark='a'/> and it starts to look like a straight line. <bookmark mark='b'/> The slope of that line is the derivative: how much the output changes, for each small change of the input.
a9c2ef9a22eb.zh: 把一条光滑的曲线放大，越凑越近，<bookmark mark='a'/>它就开始像一条直线了。<bookmark mark='b'/>这条直线的斜率就是导数：输入每有一点小小的变化，输出会跟着变化多少。

081a3a7ab454.en: Written down: f at x plus a small step h, is about f of x, plus the derivative times h. <bookmark mark='a'/> The smaller the step, the better the guess. A derivative is the best straight-line description of a function, near one point.
081a3a7ab454.zh: 写成式子：f在x加上一小步h处的值，大约等于f(x)，加上导数乘以h。<bookmark mark='a'/>步子越小，这个估计就越准。导数，就是一个函数在某一点附近最好的直线描述。

c6c9a05f6385.en: A few derivatives come up over and over. <bookmark mark='a'/> The exponential is its own derivative. <bookmark mark='b'/> The logarithm's derivative is one over x. That's why the surprise climbs so steeply as p shrinks. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the chain rule: the derivative of f of g of x is f prime at g of x, times g prime at x. Change flows through a composition, multiplying as it goes.
c6c9a05f6385.zh: 有几个导数会一再出现。<bookmark mark='a'/>指数函数的导数就是它自己。<bookmark mark='b'/>对数的导数是x分之1。正因为这样，p变小时，意外度才会升得那么陡。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有链式法则：f(g(x))的导数，等于f的导数在g(x)处的值，乘以g的导数在x处的值。变化穿过一层层复合，一路相乘。

fe3c280fd9a0.en: A loss depends on many numbers at once. With two, it's a surface over a plane. <bookmark mark='a'/> Nudge one number while holding the other still, and you get a partial derivative: the slope along that axis. <bookmark mark='b'/> Collect them all into one vector, and you have the gradient. It points straight uphill, the steepest way there is. <bookmark mark='c'/> So step the other way, again and again, and you slide down into a valley. That's gradient descent, and it trains every model in this series.
fe3c280fd9a0.zh: 损失同时取决于很多个数。如果只有两个，它就是平面上方的一张曲面。<bookmark mark='a'/>轻轻推动其中一个数，另一个保持不动，就得到一个偏导数：沿那条坐标轴的斜率。<bookmark mark='b'/>把所有偏导数收进一个向量，就得到了梯度。它指向正上坡，是最陡的那个方向。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以，朝相反的方向一步又一步地走，你就会滑进山谷。这就是梯度下降，本系列的每一个模型，都靠它来训练。

cc32d8538762.en: Seen from above, the surface becomes a map of contour lines, each at one height. <bookmark mark='a'/> The slope in any direction you choose is the dot product of the gradient with that direction, from part two. <bookmark mark='b'/> So it's largest straight along the gradient, <bookmark mark='c'/> zero along the contour line, where the height doesn't change, <bookmark mark='d'/> and most negative pointing against the gradient: downhill.
cc32d8538762.zh: 从正上方看，这张曲面就变成一张等高线图，每条线都在同一个高度上。<bookmark mark='a'/>沿你任选的一个方向，斜率都等于梯度与这个方向的点积，就是第2部分讲过的点积。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以，正对着梯度的方向，斜率最大；<bookmark mark='c'/>沿着等高线，高度不变，斜率是0；<bookmark mark='d'/>背对着梯度，斜率最负：那就是下坡。

af80ce252fc3.en: Now let a function take a whole vector to another vector, the way a layer of a network does. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's one that bends the plane: the grid lines curve. <bookmark mark='b'/> But zoom in close to any point, and the curves straighten out. Up close, every smooth map looks like a matrix: its Jacobian, the table of all its partial derivatives.
af80ce252fc3.zh: 现在，让一个函数把一整个向量变成另一个向量，就像网络的一层所做的那样。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个映射会把平面弄弯：网格线都弯曲了。<bookmark mark='b'/>但凑近任何一点放大，弯曲的线就变直了。凑近看，每个光滑的映射都像一个矩阵：它的雅可比矩阵，也就是它所有偏导数排成的表。

754860512ce5.en: The Jacobian's determinant, from part two, says how much the map stretches area near that point. <bookmark mark='a'/> And the chain rule for maps is matrix multiplication: the Jacobian of one map after another is the product of their Jacobians, each taken where its input lands.
754860512ce5.zh: 雅可比矩阵的行列式，第2部分讲过，它说明这个映射在那一点附近，把面积拉伸了多少。<bookmark mark='a'/>而映射的链式法则，就是矩阵乘法：一个映射接着另一个映射，它的雅可比矩阵，就是两者雅可比矩阵的乘积，每一个都在它的输入所落到的那一点上求出。

eb5bc0a1f7bb.en: A network is a long chain of maps, from its parameters to a single number at the end: the loss. <bookmark mark='a'/> By the chain rule, the gradient is a product of Jacobians, one for each link. <bookmark mark='b'/> The product is the same whichever end you start multiplying from. The cost is not.
eb5bc0a1f7bb.zh: 一个网络就是一长串映射，从它的参数出发，一直到末端的一个数：损失。<bookmark mark='a'/>按照链式法则，梯度就是一串雅可比矩阵的乘积，每一环一个。<bookmark mark='b'/>不管从哪一头开始乘，乘积都一样。花的力气却不一样。

c053e5b59997.en: Start from the parameters, and you carry a whole matrix along, with a column for every parameter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start from the loss, and you carry a single row: one number for each value in the layer you've reached. <bookmark mark='b'/> With one loss and a hundred million parameters, going backwards is a hundred million times less work. That's reverse-mode differentiation. Applied to neural networks, it's called backpropagation: described by Seppo Linnainmaa in 1970, and made famous by Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams in 1986.
c053e5b59997.zh: 从参数那头开始，你得一路带着一整个矩阵，每个参数占一列。<bookmark mark='a'/>从损失那头开始，你只需带着一行：你走到的那一层里，每个值对应一个数。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有一个损失，却有1亿个参数时，倒着算的工作量，只有正着算的1亿分之一。这就是反向模式求导。用在神经网络上，它叫作反向传播：1970年，塞波·林纳因马描述了它；1986年，鲁梅尔哈特、辛顿和威廉姆斯让它广为人知。

b28cf0105622.en: Let's run it by hand, on the smallest network there is: one input, one weight, one bias, a squashing function, and a squared error. <bookmark mark='a'/> Forwards first: the values flow from left to right, and end in the loss, 0.854.
b28cf0105622.zh: 我们来手算一遍，用的是最小的网络：一个输入，一个权重，一个偏置，一个S形函数，再加一个平方误差。<bookmark mark='a'/>先向前算：数值从左往右流动，最后得到损失，0.854。

9df46440a916.en: Now backwards. Start at the loss, with a gradient of one, and walk back. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each step multiplies the gradient arriving from the right by its own local derivative, and passes the result to the left. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the weight, the gradient is minus 0.259: raise the weight a little, and the loss falls by about a quarter as much. No step needed to know anything but its own derivative.
9df46440a916.zh: 现在往回算。从损失出发，梯度是1，然后一步步往回走。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一步都把从右边传来的梯度，乘以它自己的局部导数，再把结果传给左边。<bookmark mark='b'/>到了权重这里，梯度是负0.259：把权重调高一点点，损失就会下降，降幅大约是这一点的四分之一。每一步除了自己的导数，什么都不需要知道。

e81f4067b1cf.en: One more rule. When a value feeds into two places, <bookmark mark='a'/> the gradients coming back from both are added together. <bookmark mark='b'/> That's the whole algorithm: visit the nodes in reverse order, and let each one pass its gradient back to its inputs.
e81f4067b1cf.zh: 还有一条规则。当一个值同时流向两个地方，<bookmark mark='a'/>从这两处传回来的梯度，要加在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>整个算法就是这些：按相反的顺序访问各个节点，让每个节点把它的梯度，传回给它的输入。

8a89fb34e36b.en: Chapter six. The machine, in code.
8a89fb34e36b.zh: 第6章。用代码写出这台机器。

67ea31515972.en: Here it is in code: the series' own automatic differentiation, about a hundred and fifty lines in all. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every operation remembers its inputs, along with a small function that sends a gradient back to each one. Here's multiplication: the gradient for one input is the incoming gradient, times the other input. <bookmark mark='b'/> And backward visits the graph in reverse order, adds up what arrives at each node, and passes it on.
67ea31515972.zh: 这就是它的代码：本系列自己的自动微分，一共大约150行。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个运算都记住它的输入，还附带一个小函数，负责把梯度传回给每个输入。这是乘法：一个输入得到的梯度，等于传进来的梯度，乘以另一个输入。<bookmark mark='b'/>而backward函数按相反的顺序遍历这张图，把到达每个节点的梯度加起来，再继续往回传。

fbee478aa97c.en: Does it work? <bookmark mark='a'/> Nudge each number by a millionth, measure how much the loss changes, and compare: the gradients agree to ten decimal places. <bookmark mark='b'/> Against PyTorch, the library most of today's models are trained with, they agree to sixteen, the limit of the computer's own arithmetic.
fbee478aa97c.zh: 它管用吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个数推动百万分之一，测一测损失变了多少，再拿来比较：两种梯度直到小数点后10位都一致。<bookmark mark='b'/>再和PyTorch比，当今大多数模型都是用这个库训练的：两者一致到16位，这已经是计算机自身算术精度的极限。

b3627cdc7c3c.en: Now let's use it. In part one, counting letter pairs got us to 3.33 bits per letter. <bookmark mark='a'/> This time, nothing is counted. The model has 729 adjustable scores, one for every pair of letters, all starting at zero, and our library trains them by gradient descent on the books.
b3627cdc7c3c.zh: 现在来用它。在第1部分，统计字母对，让我们做到了每个字母3.33比特。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一次，什么都不数。模型有729个可调的分数，每一对字母一个，全都从0开始，由我们的库在那些书上，用梯度下降来训练。

bf64301d3f9b.en: The loss falls fast, then settles: at 3.33 bits, the counting answer. <bookmark mark='a'/> And the scores themselves have become the logarithms of the counts. That's maximum likelihood again, reached by walking downhill instead of by counting. <bookmark mark='b'/> The same loop, with more numbers and better models, trains everything else in this series.
bf64301d3f9b.zh: 损失先是快速下降，然后稳定下来：停在3.33比特，正是计数得到的答案。<bookmark mark='a'/>而这些分数本身，也变成了计数的对数。这又是最大似然，只不过这次是一路下山走到的，而不是数出来的。<bookmark mark='b'/>同样的这个循环，换上更多的数、更好的模型，就能训练本系列里其余的一切。

12bed290f8f4.en: The gradient says which way is downhill. It doesn't say how the slope itself is changing. <bookmark mark='a'/> That's the second derivative: curvature. With many inputs, it's a matrix of second derivatives, the Hessian. <bookmark mark='b'/> It's symmetric, so, from part two, it has perpendicular eigenvectors: the directions of pure curvature. Its eigenvalues say how sharply the surface bends along each. <bookmark mark='c'/> Both positive: a bowl. One negative: a saddle, downhill one way and uphill the other. In many dimensions, most of the flat spots a model passes are saddles, not valleys.
12bed290f8f4.zh: 梯度告诉你哪边是下坡，却没告诉你，斜率本身在怎样变化。<bookmark mark='a'/>那是二阶导数：曲率。有多个输入时，它是一个由二阶导数组成的矩阵，叫作黑塞矩阵。<bookmark mark='b'/>它是对称的，所以按第2部分讲的，它有互相垂直的特征向量：也就是纯粹弯曲的方向。它的特征值，说明曲面沿每个方向弯得有多厉害。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个都为正：是一个碗。一个为负：是一个鞍点，一个方向下坡，另一个方向上坡。在很多维的空间里，模型经过的平坦之处，大多是鞍点，而不是山谷。

41d8e987ac71.en: Curvature explains why plain gradient descent can be slow. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a long, narrow valley, bent twenty-five times more sharply across than along, the steepest way down points mostly at the opposite wall. So the steps zigzag from wall to wall, and crawl along the floor. <bookmark mark='b'/> Momentum, carrying some speed from step to step, does better. <bookmark mark='c'/> Newton's method uses the curvature itself to rescale the step, and in a bowl like this lands at the bottom in one jump. <bookmark mark='d'/> For a model with billions of numbers the full Hessian is far too big to use, but the problem it reveals shapes every modern optimizer, in part nine.
41d8e987ac71.zh: 曲率解释了，为什么单纯的梯度下降可能很慢。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一条又长又窄的山谷里，横向的弯曲程度是纵向的25倍，最陡的下坡方向，大多指向对面的谷壁。于是每一步都在两边谷壁之间来回折返，沿着谷底慢慢往前爬。<bookmark mark='b'/>动量，也就是把一部分速度从这一步带到下一步，效果更好。<bookmark mark='c'/>牛顿法直接用曲率本身来重新缩放每一步，在这样一个碗里，一步就跳到谷底。<bookmark mark='d'/>对一个有几十亿个数的模型来说，完整的黑塞矩阵太大了，根本用不上；但它揭示的问题，塑造了每一个现代优化器，这些到第9部分再讲。

677ddfc14125.en: Let's take stock. Zoom in on a smooth function and it becomes a straight line, whose slope is the derivative. With many inputs, the slopes form the gradient, which points uphill. Up close, a map between spaces is a matrix, its Jacobian, and the chain rule multiplies those matrices. Multiplying them from the loss backwards is cheap, and that's backpropagation. We built it in a few lines, checked it, and trained a model with it. And curvature told us why going downhill can still be slow.
677ddfc14125.zh: 我们来盘点一下。把一个光滑的函数放大，它就变成一条直线，直线的斜率就是导数。有多个输入时，各个斜率组成梯度，它指向上坡。凑近看，空间之间的映射就是一个矩阵，也就是它的雅可比矩阵，而链式法则把这些矩阵相乘。从损失那头倒着乘，代价很小，这就是反向传播。我们用寥寥几行代码把它搭了出来，检验了它，还用它训练了一个模型。最后，曲率告诉我们，为什么下山仍然可能很慢。

deeb15005689.en: This is the engine of everything that follows. Our library trains the first neural network of the series in part eight, and the chain of Jacobians through a deep network decides whether it can learn at all. Curvature, valleys and saddles come back when we build better optimizers, in part nine.
deeb15005689.zh: 这是后面一切的引擎。在第8部分，我们的库会训练本系列的第一个神经网络，而贯穿一个深度网络的那一串雅可比矩阵，决定了它到底能不能学得起来。曲率、山谷和鞍点，会在第9部分我们搭建更好的优化器时再次出现。

7b55e042ca1f.en: Next time: randomness. Probability distributions that move, random walks that become Brownian motion, and the noise that diffusion models learn to undo. <bookmark mark='a'/> It's the last piece of mathematics we need before the models themselves.
7b55e042ca1f.zh: 下一次：随机性。会动的概率分布，变成布朗运动的随机游走，还有扩散模型学着去消除的噪声。<bookmark mark='a'/>在进入模型本身之前，这是我们需要的最后一块数学。

3799521aa094.en: Griewank and Walther's Evaluating Derivatives is the book on automatic differentiation, and Baydin's survey is a good place to start. Thanks for watching, and see you in part four.
3799521aa094.zh: 格里万克和瓦尔特的《计算导数》，是自动微分方面的权威著作，而拜丁的综述，是很好的入门。感谢观看，第4部分见。
